description: An aspiring quantitative analyst who feels confident in discrete math but is intimidated by C++ memory management and low-level system details.

nodes.description: A focused review of C++ memory management, including pointers and references, to bridge the gap from general programming to C++ specific syntax.
nodes.title: Pointers and References Refresher
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student has some prior exposure to C++ but requires a specific bridge to master manual memory management and pointer logic before the core data structures are introduced.
Building on their some_prior_exposure, this node ensures foundational mastery of C++ templates and OOD which are vital for implementing generic data structures.
nodes.title: C++ Foundations & OOD
nodes.description: Object-oriented design in C++, covering class structures, inheritance, templates, and exception handling for robust software design.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node reinforces recursion and linked lists, essential topics for a student with some_prior_exposure to prepare for more complex nested structures.
nodes.title: Lists and Recursion Fundamentals
nodes.description: Implementation of singly and doubly linked lists, along with the fundamental principles of recursion and its role in data structure navigation.
Assesses understanding of recursion, list implementations, and Big-O asymptotic analysis.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Analysis
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard assessment for the some_prior_exposure tier to ensure competency in algorithm analysis before moving to sequence structures.

nodes.title: Stacks, Queues, and Deques
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement for all students to master basic linear ADTs used throughout the course.
nodes.description: Introduction to LIFO and FIFO structures, focusing on stack and queue ADTs and their C++ implementations.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Ensures the student can bridge the gap between static arrays and more flexible sequence containers in C++.
nodes.title: Vectors and Iterators
nodes.description: Exploring dynamic arrays (Vectors), the iterator pattern, and basic sequence-based sorting like Bubble Sort.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard checkpoint to verify mastery of sequence structures for a student with some_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: Quiz 2: Sequence Structures
nodes.description: Assesses proficiency in sequence-based structures and iterator logic.
Comprehensive review session covering all material from C++ foundations through sequence-based structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory midterm review to consolidate knowledge for students of all tiers, including some_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: Midterm Review Checkpoint

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core material necessary for understanding non-linear hierarchical data structures.
nodes.title: General Trees
nodes.description: General tree definitions, terminology, and implementation strategies in C++.
Depth-first and breadth-first traversal algorithms for binary and general trees.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Fundamental tree algorithms required for the cumulative final and subsequent tree-based topics.
nodes.title: Tree Traversal Algorithms

nodes.personalizationRationale: Crucial core content for efficient sorting and priority management, tailored for students at the some_prior_exposure level.
nodes.title: Priority Queues and Heaps
nodes.description: Implementation of Priority Queues using binary heaps, focusing on the heap-order and complete-tree properties.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core material on associative containers, essential for understanding C++ STL map/unordered_map.
nodes.title: Maps and Hash Tables
nodes.description: Design and implementation of Maps and Hash Tables, including hash functions and collision resolution strategies.
Testing knowledge on hashing mechanics, skip lists, and dictionary ADTs.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard assessment to ensure the student has mastered efficient lookup structures.
nodes.title: Quiz 3: Hashing & Dictionaries
BST and AVL Trees
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required core theory for understanding self-balancing trees, a key learning objective for this cumulative course.
nodes.description: Exploring Binary Search Trees (BST) and the mechanics of AVL tree rotations to maintain balance.

nodes.title: Multi-way and Red-Black Trees
nodes.personalizationRationale: Complex theory-heavy content required for all students to understand high-performance search trees.
nodes.description: In-depth look at (2,4) Trees and Red-Black Trees, emphasizing their structural properties and performance.
Analysis and implementation of efficient sorting algorithms including Merge Sort and Selection Sort.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Fundamental sorting proficiency required for the final exam and real-world algorithm design.
nodes.title: Sorting Algorithms

nodes.description: Final quiz covering sorting and advanced data structure topics.
nodes.title: Quiz 4: Advanced Topics
nodes.personalizationRationale: Assessment checkpoint to ensure sorting concepts are mastered before the cumulative final review.
Mandatory comprehensive review to prepare for the 30% final exam, covering all topics for the some_prior_exposure tier.
nodes.title: Final Cumulative Review
nodes.description: Cumulative review of the entire syllabus, focusing on choosing the right structure for specific problem constraints.
